【DB_ID】 card_games
【Schema】
# Table: cards
[
(id:INTEGER, unique id number identifying the cards: -, Primary Key, Examples: [41138, 1349, 23810]),
(artist:TEXT, : The name of the artist that illustrated the card art.-, Examples: [Pete Venters, Volkan Baǵa, Justin Sweet]),
(asciiName:TEXT, ascii Name: The ASCII(opens new window) (Basic/128) code formatted card name with no special unicode characters.-, Examples: [El-Hajjaj, Junun Efreet, Dandan]),
(availability:TEXT, : A list of the card's available printing types.-"arena", "dreamcast", "mtgo", "paper", "shandalar", Examples: [mtgo,paper, paper, arena]),
(borderColor:TEXT, border Color: The color of the card border.-"black", "borderless", "gold", "silver", "white", Examples: [black, white, borderless]),
(cardKingdomFoilId:TEXT, card Kingdom Foil Id: card Kingdom Foil Id-cardKingdomFoilId, when paired with cardKingdomId that is not Null, is incredibly powerful., Examples: [123094, 123095, 123096]),
(cardKingdomId:TEXT, card Kingdom Id: card Kingdom Id-A list of all the colors in the color indicator, Examples: [122719, 122720, 122725]),
(colorIdentity:TEXT, color Identity: A list of all the colors found in manaCost, colorIndicator, and text-, Examples: [W, B, U]),
(colorIndicator:TEXT, color Indicator: A list of all the colors in the color indicator (The symbol prefixed to a card's types).-, Examples: [U, G, R]),
(colors:TEXT, : A list of all the colors in manaCost and colorIndicator.-Some cards may not have values, such as cards with "Devoid" in its text., Examples: [W, B, U]),
(convertedManaCost:REAL, converted Mana Cost: The converted mana cost of the card. Use the manaValue property.-if value is higher, it means that this card cost more converted mana, Examples: [7.0, 5.0, 4.0]),
(duelDeck:TEXT, duel Deck: The indicator for which duel deck the card is in.-, Examples: [a, b]),
(edhrecRank:INTEGER, rec Rank in edh: The card rank on EDHRec-, Examples: [15650, 12702, 11081]),
(faceConvertedManaCost:REAL, face Converted Mana Cost: The converted mana cost or mana value for the face for either half or part of the card.-if value is higher, it means that this card cost more converted mana for the face, Examples: [4.0, 5.0, 6.0]),
(faceName:TEXT, face Name: The name on the face of the card.-, Examples: [Dusk, Dawn, Commit]),
(flavorName:TEXT, flavor Name: The promotional card name printed above the true card name on special cards that has no game function.-The promotional card name printed above the true card name on special cards that has no game function., Examples: [Godzilla, King of the Monsters]),
(flavorText:TEXT, flavor Text: The italicized text found below the rules text that has no game function.-The italicized text found below the rules text that has no game function.),
(frameEffects:TEXT, frame Effects: The visual frame effects.-"colorshifted", "companion", "compasslanddfc", "devoid", "draft", "etched", "extendedart", "fullart", "inverted", "legendary", "lesson", "miracle", "mooneldrazidfc", "nyxtouched", "originpwdfc", "showcase", "snow", "sunmoondfc", "textless", "tombstone", "waxingandwaningmoondfc", Examples: [legendary, nyxtouched, miracle]),
(frameVersion:TEXT, frame Version: The version of the card frame style.-"1993", "1997", "2003", "2015", "future", Examples: [2003, 1993, 2015]),
(hand:TEXT, : The starting maximum hand size total modifier.-A + or - character precedes an integer.   positive maximum hand size: +1, +2, .... negative maximum hand size: -1, .... neural maximum hand size: 0...., Examples: [1, 0, -2]),
(hasAlternativeDeckLimit:INTEGER, has Alternative Deck Limit: If the card allows a value other than 4 copies in a deck.-0: disallow 1: allow, Examples: [0, 1]),
(hasContentWarning:INTEGER, has Content Warning: If the card marked by Wizards of the Coast (opens new window) for having sensitive content. See this official article (opens new window) for more information.-0: doesn't have 1: has sensitve content or Wizards of the Coast  Cards with this property may have missing or degraded properties and values., Examples: [0, 1]),
(hasFoil:INTEGER, has Foil: If the card can be found in foil-0: cannot be found 1: can be found, Examples: [0, 1]),
(hasNonFoil:INTEGER, has Non Foil: If the card can be found in non-foil-0: cannot be found 1: can be found, Examples: [1, 0]),
(isAlternative:INTEGER, is Alternative: If the card is an alternate variation to an original printing-0: is not 1: is, Examples: [0, 1]),
(isFullArt:INTEGER, is Full Art: If the card has full artwork.-0: doesn't have, 1: has full artwork, Examples: [0, 1]),
(isOnlineOnly:INTEGER, is Online Only: If the card is only available in online game variations.-0: is not 1: is, Examples: [0, 1]),
(isOversized:INTEGER, is Oversized: If the card is oversized.-0: is not 1: is, Examples: [0, 1]),
(isPromo:INTEGER, is Promotion: If the card is a promotional printing.-0: is not 1: is, Examples: [0, 1]),
(isReprint:INTEGER, is Reprint: If the card has been reprinted.-0: has not 1: has not been, Examples: [1, 0]),
(isReserved:INTEGER, is Reserved: If the card is on the Magic: The Gathering Reserved List (opens new window)-If the card is on the Magic, it will appear in The Gathering Reserved List, Examples: [0, 1]),
(isStarter:INTEGER, is Starter: If the card is found in a starter deck such as Planeswalker/Brawl decks.-0: is not 1: is, Examples: [0, 1]),
(isStorySpotlight:INTEGER, is Story Spotlight: If the card is a Story Spotlight card.-0: is not 1: is, Examples: [0, 1]),
(isTextless:INTEGER, is Text less: If the card does not have a text box.-0: has a text box; 1: doesn't have a text box;, Examples: [0, 1]),
(isTimeshifted:INTEGER, is Time shifted: If the card is time shifted-If the card is "timeshifted", a feature of certain sets where a card will have a different frameVersion., Examples: [0, 1]),
(keywords:TEXT, : A list of keywords found on the card.-, Examples: [First strike, Flying, First strike,Flash]),
(layout:TEXT, : The type of card layout. For a token card, this will be "token"-, Examples: [normal, aftermath, split]),
(leadershipSkills:TEXT, leadership Skills: A list of formats the card is legal to be a commander in-),
(life:TEXT, : The starting life total modifier. A plus or minus character precedes an integer.-, Examples: [-5, -1, 2]),
(loyalty:TEXT, : The starting loyalty value of the card.-Used only on cards with "Planeswalker" in its types. empty means unkown, Examples: [6, 3, 4]),
(manaCost:TEXT, mana Cost: The mana cost of the card wrapped in brackets for each value.-manaCost is unconverted mana cost, Examples: [{5}{W}{W}, {4}{W}, {3}{W}]),
(mcmId:TEXT, : -, Examples: [16165, 16166, 16171]),
(mcmMetaId:TEXT, : -, Examples: [156, 176, 368]),
(mtgArenaId:TEXT, : -, Examples: [74983, 74986, 74987]),
(mtgjsonV4Id:TEXT, : -, Examples: [ad41be73-582f-58ed-abd4-a88c1f616ac3]),
(mtgoFoilId:TEXT, : -, Examples: [27501, 26993, 27473]),
(mtgoId:TEXT, : -, Examples: [27500, 26992, 27472]),
(multiverseId:TEXT, : -, Examples: [130550, 129465, 129470]),
(name:TEXT, : The name of the card.-Cards with multiple faces, like "Split" and "Meld" cards are given a delimiter., Examples: [Ancestor's Chosen, Angel of Mercy, Aven Cloudchaser]),
(number:TEXT, : The number of the card-, Examples: [1, 2, 7]),
(originalReleaseDate:TEXT, : original Release Date-The original release date in ISO 8601(opens new window) format for a promotional card printed outside of a cycle window, such as Secret Lair Drop promotions., Examples: [2012/12/1, 2006/12/1, 2007/12/1]),
(originalText:TEXT, : original Text-The text on the card as originally printed.),
(originalType:TEXT, : original Type-The type of the card as originally printed. Includes any supertypes and subtypes., Examples: [Creature - Human Cleric]),
(otherFaceIds:TEXT, : other Face Ids-A list of card UUID's to this card's counterparts, such as transformed or melded faces., Examples: [87f0062a-8321-5c16-960e-a12ce1df5839]),
(power:TEXT, : The power of the card.-∞ means infinite power null or * refers to unknown power, Examples: [4, 3, 2]),
(printings:TEXT, : A list of set printing codes the card was printed in, formatted in uppercase.-),
(promoTypes:TEXT, promo Types: A list of promotional types for a card.-"arenaleague", "boosterfun", "boxtopper", "brawldeck", "bundle", "buyabox", "convention", "datestamped", "draculaseries", "draftweekend", "duels", "event", "fnm", "gameday", "gateway", "giftbox", "gilded", "godzillaseries", "instore", "intropack", "jpwalker", "judgegift", "league", "mediainsert", "neonink", "openhouse", "planeswalkerstamped", "playerrewards", "playpromo", "premiereshop", "prerelease", "promopack", "release", "setpromo", "stamped", "textured", "themepack", "thick", "tourney", "wizardsplaynetwork", Examples: [boxtopper,boosterfun, boosterfun, release,buyabox]),
(purchaseUrls:TEXT, purchase Urls: Links that navigate to websites where the card can be purchased.-),
(rarity:TEXT, : The card printing rarity.-, Examples: [uncommon, common, rare]),
(scryfallId:TEXT, : -, Examples: [7a5cd03c-4227-4551-aa4b-7d119f0468b5]),
(scryfallIllustrationId:TEXT, : -, Examples: [be2f7173-c8b7-4172-a388-9b2c6b3c16e5]),
(scryfallOracleId:TEXT, : -, Examples: [fc2ccab7-cab1-4463-b73d-898070136d74]),
(setCode:TEXT, Set Code: The set printing code that the card is from.-, Examples: [10E, 2ED, 2XM]),

schema_representation.execution_plan: Execution plan: The question asks for the foreign name and the type of a card that has an 'abzan' watermark. To achieve this, I need to: 1) Select cards that have 'abzan' as their watermark. The `watermark` column in the `cards` table is necessary for this filtering. 2) Retrieve the `name` from the `foreign_data` table, which represents the foreign name of the card. This requires joining `cards` and `foreign_data` tables on their common `uuid` column. 3) Retrieve the `type` of the card from the `cards` table. Therefore, `cards.watermark`, `cards.type`, `cards.uuid`, `foreign_data.name`, and `foreign_data.uuid` are essential. The `uuid` columns are needed for the join operation.

sql_exec_info.sql: SELECT T2.name, T1.type FROM cards AS T1 INNER JOIN foreign_data AS T2 ON T1.uuid = T2.uuid WHERE T1.watermark = 'abzan'

schema_representation.execution_plan: Execution plan: The question asks for the foreign name and the type of a card that has an 'abzan' watermark. To achieve this, I need to: 1) Select cards that have 'abzan' as their watermark. The `watermark` column in the `cards` table is necessary for this filtering. 2) Retrieve the `name` from the `foreign_data` table, which represents the foreign name of the card. This requires joining `cards` and `foreign_data` tables on their common `uuid` column. 3) Retrieve the `type` of the card from the `cards` table. Therefore, `cards.watermark`, `cards.type`, `cards.uuid`, `foreign_data.name`, and `foreign_data.uuid` are essential. The `uuid` columns are needed for the join operation.

selected_schemas.chain_of_thought_reasoning: To answer this question, I need to find the release date of the set containing the card named 'Ancestor's Chosen'. The 'name' column in the 'cards' table is needed to identify the card. I don't see releaseDate in any of the tables. I will try to find the set code of the card, so I can look for the set in the sets table and then look for the release date. I don't see any release date in the sets table either, so I will look into the set_translations table. The set_translations table has the setCode and translation of the card set.

The question asks for the release date of a set that contains a card named 'Ancestor's Chosen'. The `cards` table contains the `name` of the cards and a `cardSetId` which links to the `sets` table. The `sets` table contains the `releaseDate` and the `code` which is the `cardSetId` from the `cards` table. Therefore, I need to join `cards` and `sets` tables using `cardSetId` and `code` respectively, filter by `name` in the `cards` table, and select `releaseDate` from the `sets` table.

sql_exec_info.sql: SELECT T2.releaseDate FROM cards AS T1 INNER JOIN sets AS T2 ON T1.setCode = T2.code WHERE T1.name = 'Ancestor''s Chosen'

selected_schemas.chain_of_thought_reasoning: To answer this question, I need to: 1) Filter the 'cards' table for cards with converted mana cost greater than 5, 2) Filter the 'cards' table for cards with unknown power, 3) Identify the set 'Coldsnap' and join this information with the cards table. The name of the card set is needed to identify the set. The faceConvertedManaCost is needed to filter for cards with a converted mana cost greater than 5. The power is needed to filter for cards with unknown power. The name column of the sets table is needed to filter for the 'Coldsnap' set. The set code is needed to join the sets table with the cards table (though not explicitly stated in the question).

The question asks to count cards from a specific set ('Coldsnap') that have a converted mana cost greater than 5 and an unknown power. Therefore, I need to: 1) Identify cards belonging to the 'Coldsnap' set. This requires joining `cards` and `sets` tables. The `sets.name` column will be used to filter for 'Coldsnap'. 2) Filter these cards by `faceConvertedManaCost` greater than 5. 3) Filter these cards further by `power` being unknown (represented by '*' or NULL). The `cards.faceConvertedManaCost` and `cards.power` columns are directly used for filtering. The `cards.uuid` and `sets.code` are needed for the join condition.

sql_exec_info.sql: SELECT COUNT(T1.id) FROM cards AS T1 INNER JOIN sets AS T2 ON T1.setCode = T2.code WHERE T2.name = 'Coldsnap' AND T1.convertedManaCost > 5 AND (T1.power = '*' OR T1.power IS NULL)

selected_schemas.chain_of_thought_reasoning: To answer this question, I need to: 1) Find the set named 'Coldsnap', 2) Find the Italian text ruling for the cards in that set. The 'name' column in the 'sets' table is needed to identify the set 'Coldsnap'. The 'language' and 'text' columns in the 'foreign_data' table are needed to retrieve the Italian text ruling.

The question asks for the Italian text ruling of cards in the 'Coldsnap' set. This requires joining the 'sets' table with the 'foreign_data' table to filter by set name and language, and then retrieve the ruling text. The 'sets' table is needed to filter by the set name 'Coldsnap'. The 'foreign_data' table is needed to filter by the language 'Italian' and to retrieve the 'text' which represents the ruling. The 'uuid' column is needed to join 'sets' and 'foreign_data' tables.

sql_exec_info.sql: SELECT T1.text FROM foreign_data AS T1 INNER JOIN cards AS T2 ON T1.uuid = T2.uuid INNER JOIN sets AS T3 ON T2.setCode = T3.code WHERE T1.language = 'Italian' AND T3.name = 'Coldsnap'

selected_schemas.chain_of_thought_reasoning: To answer this question, I need to: 1) Filter for cards in the 'Coldsnap' set, 2) Find the cards with the highest face converted mana cost, 3) Find the Italian names of these cards. The set name is needed to filter the cards, the faceConvertedManaCost is needed to determine the highest converted mana cost, and the language and name are needed to find the Italian names.

The question asks for the Italian names of cards from the 'Coldsnap' set that have the highest converted mana cost. I need to: 1) Identify the set with the name 'Coldsnap'. This requires the `name` column in the `sets` table. 2) Find the cards associated with this set. Although there isn't a direct foreign key linking `cards` to `sets` in the provided schema, the question implies a relationship. I will assume `cardKingdomId` in `cards` relates to `code` in `sets`. 3) Filter these cards to find the one with the highest `faceConvertedManaCost`. This requires the `faceConvertedManaCost` column in the `cards` table. 4) Retrieve the Italian name for these cards. This requires joining with the `foreign_data` table and filtering by `language = 'Italian'`, using the `language` and `name` columns from `foreign_data`. The `uuid` column in `foreign_data` will be used to join with `cards`.

sql_exec_info.sql: SELECT T1.name FROM foreign_data AS T1 WHERE T1.language = 'Italian' AND T1.uuid IN (SELECT T2.uuid FROM cards AS T2 INNER JOIN sets AS T3 ON T2.setCode = T3.code WHERE T3.name = 'Coldsnap' AND T2.convertedManaCost = (SELECT MAX(T4.convertedManaCost) FROM cards AS T4 INNER JOIN sets AS T5 ON T4.setCode = T5.code WHERE T5.name = 'Coldsnap'))

schema_representation.execution_plan: Execution plan: To answer this question, I need to: 1) Filter for cards in the 'Coldsnap' set, 2) Find the cards with the highest face converted mana cost, 3) Find the Italian names of these cards. The set name is needed to filter the cards, the faceConvertedManaCost is needed to determine the highest converted mana cost, and the language and name are needed to find the Italian names.

sql_exec_info.sql:
SELECT T1.name
        FROM foreign_data AS T1
        INNER JOIN cards AS T2
          ON T1.uuid = T2.uuid
        INNER JOIN sets AS T3
          ON T2.setCode = T3.code
        WHERE
          T1.language = 'Italian' AND T3.name = 'Coldsnap' AND T2.convertedManaCost = (
            SELECT MAX(T4.convertedManaCost)
            FROM cards AS T4
            INNER JOIN sets AS T5
              ON T4.setCode = T5.code
            WHERE
              T5.name = 'Coldsnap'
          );

selected_schemas.chain_of_thought_reasoning: To answer this question, I need to find cards without multiple faces (identified by the absence of otherFaceIds), determine the highest faceConvertedManaCost among these cards, and then identify the artist for the card with the highest cost. The artist and faceConvertedManaCost columns are directly needed, and otherFaceIds is needed for filtering.

The question asks for the illustrator (artist) of the card art with the highest converted mana cost, excluding cards with multiple faces. The hint clarifies that 'doesn't have multiple faces' refers to a condition where the 'side' is NULL. However, looking at the schema, there is no 'side' column. I will assume that 'otherFaceIds' being NULL or empty implies a single-faced card, as it's the closest available indicator in the schema. Therefore, I need to find the maximum 'faceConvertedManaCost' from the 'cards' table, filter for cards where 'otherFaceIds' is NULL (or empty, assuming this indicates a single face), and then retrieve the 'artist' for that card.

sql_exec_info.sql: SELECT T1.artist FROM cards AS T1 WHERE T1.side IS NULL ORDER BY T1.convertedManaCost DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 1

selected_schemas.chain_of_thought_reasoning: To answer this question, I need to find the oldest mythic card and its legal play formats. This requires filtering for rarity 'mythic', identifying the oldest card, and then looking up its legal formats. The 'cards' table contains card information, including rarity, and the 'legalities' table contains format and status information. The 'cards' table does not contain the 'originalReleaseDate', so that column is not needed.

The question asks for the release date of the oldest 'mythic' card and its legal play formats. To find the oldest card, I need to filter by rarity and find the minimum release date. To get the legal play formats, I need to join with the 'legalities' table and filter by status. The 'cards' table contains rarity and release date information, while the 'legalities' table contains format and status information. The 'uuid' column is necessary to join these two tables.

sql_exec_info.sql:
SELECT
  T1.originalReleaseDate,
  T2.format
FROM cards AS T1
INNER JOIN legalities AS T2
  ON T1.uuid = T2.uuid
WHERE
  T1.uuid = (
    SELECT
      uuid
    FROM cards
    WHERE
      rarity = 'mythic'
    ORDER BY
      originalReleaseDate ASC NULLS LAST
    LIMIT 1
  ) AND T2.status = 'Legal';

sql_exec_info.sql: SELECT T1.originalReleaseDate, T2.format FROM cards AS T1 INNER JOIN legalities AS T2 ON T1.uuid = T2.uuid WHERE T1.uuid = (SELECT uuid FROM cards WHERE rarity = 'mythic' ORDER BY originalReleaseDate ASC NULLS LAST LIMIT 1) AND T2.status = 'Legal'

sql_exec_info.sql:
SELECT
  T1.originalReleaseDate,
  T2.format
FROM cards AS T1
INNER JOIN legalities AS T2
  ON T1.uuid = T2.uuid
WHERE

      rarity = 'mythic'

      originalReleaseDate ASC NULLS LAST

selected_schemas.chain_of_thought_reasoning: To answer the question, I need to find the artist who illustrated the least number of cards and then list the formats those cards are legal in. This requires identifying the artist, counting the cards per artist, and then linking the artist to the legal formats. The artist column is needed to identify the illustrators. The format column is needed to list the formats.

The question asks for the illustrator (artist) who illustrated the least amount of cards and the formats of those cards. To find the artist who illustrated the least amount of cards, I need to count the number of cards illustrated by each artist. The `cards` table contains the `artist` column. To find the formats of the cards illustrated by that artist, I need to join the `cards` table with the `legalities` table using their common `uuid` column, and then filter by the `artist` identified as illustrating the least cards. The `legalities` table contains the `format` column.

sql_exec_info.sql: SELECT DISTINCT T2.format FROM cards AS T1 INNER JOIN legalities AS T2 ON T1.uuid = T2.uuid WHERE T1.artist = (SELECT artist FROM cards GROUP BY artist ORDER BY COUNT(id) ASC LIMIT 1)

schema_representation.execution_plan: Execution plan: To answer the question, I need to find the artist who illustrated the least number of cards and then list the formats those cards are legal in. This requires identifying the artist, counting the cards per artist, and then linking the artist to the legal formats. The artist column is needed to identify the illustrators. The format column is needed to list the formats.

sql_exec_info.sql:
SELECT
  T1.artist,
  T2.format
FROM cards AS T1
INNER JOIN legalities AS T2
  ON T1.uuid = T2.uuid
WHERE
  T1.artist = (
    SELECT
      artist
    FROM cards
    GROUP BY
      artist
    ORDER BY
      COUNT(uuid) ASC
    LIMIT 1
  )
GROUP BY
  T1.artist,
  T2.format;

selected_schemas.chain_of_thought_reasoning: To answer this question, I need to find set names that have Korean translations but not Japanese translations. This requires checking the `set_translations` table for the presence of both Korean and the absence of Japanese translations and then joining with the `sets` table to get the set names. The `sets` table is needed to get the set names. The `set_translations` table is needed to filter by language.

The question asks to find sets that have Korean translation but do not have Japanese translation. This requires checking the 'set_translations' table for the 'language' column to filter for 'Korean' and exclude 'Japanese'. The 'sets' table is needed to get the 'name' of the sets. Therefore, I need 'language' and 'translation' from 'set_translations' to identify the translations, and 'name' from 'sets' to list the set names. The 'setCode' in 'set_translations' will be used to join with the 'code' in 'sets' to link translations to set names.

sql_exec_info.sql: SELECT T1.name FROM sets AS T1 WHERE T1.code IN (SELECT setCode FROM set_translations WHERE language = 'Korean') AND T1.code NOT IN (SELECT setCode FROM set_translations WHERE language LIKE '%Japanese%')

Then I need to use the users table to get the DisplayName and WebsiteUrl associated with the user who has the highest bounty amount.

The question asks for the display names and website URLs of users who received the highest bounty amount under vote type 8. This requires joining the 'votes' table with the 'users' table. From the 'votes' table, I need 'VoteTypeId' to filter for type 8, 'BountyAmount' to find the maximum bounty, and 'UserId' to link to the 'users' table. From the 'users' table, I need 'Id' to join with 'votes.UserId', 'DisplayName' to display the user's name, and 'WebsiteUrl' to display their website URL.

sql_exec_info.sql: SELECT T1.DisplayName, T1.WebsiteUrl FROM users AS T1 INNER JOIN votes AS T2 ON T1.Id = T2.UserId WHERE T2.VoteTypeId = 8 ORDER BY T2.BountyAmount DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 1

alignment.value_description: Alignment refers to a character's moral and ethical stance and can be used to describe the overall attitude or behavior of a superhero. Some common alignments for superheroes include: Good: These superheroes are typically kind, selfless, and dedicated to protecting others and upholding justice. The question asks for the full names of superheroes with over 15 super powers. To achieve this, I need to: 1) Identify superheroes and their names from the 'superhero' table. 2) Count the number of super powers associated with each superhero. This requires joining 'superhero' with 'hero_power' on 'hero_id' and then counting the 'power_id' for each 'hero_id'. 3) Filter these counts to include only those superheroes with more than 15 powers. The 'superhero_name' column is needed for the output. The 'hero_id' in both 'superhero' and 'hero_power' tables is essential for joining. The 'power_id' in the 'hero_power' table is needed to count the number of powers.

sql_exec_info.sql:
SELECT T1.full_name
FROM superhero AS T1
INNER JOIN hero_power AS T2
  ON T1.id = T2.hero_id
GROUP BY
  T1.id,
  T1.full_name
HAVING
  COUNT(T2.power_id) > 15;

The question asks for the full name of the tallest hero published by Marvel Comics. To find the tallest hero, I need to identify the maximum height, which is in the `height_cm` column of the `superhero` table. To filter for heroes published by 'Marvel Comics', I need to join the `superhero` table with the `publisher` table using `publisher_id` and filter by `publisher_name`. The `superhero_name` column is needed to return the full name of the hero.

sql_exec_info.sql:
SELECT T1.full_name
FROM superhero AS T1
INNER JOIN publisher AS T2
  ON T1.publisher_id = T2.id
WHERE
  T2.publisher_name = 'Marvel Comics' AND T1.height_cm > 0
ORDER BY
  T1.height_cm DESC
LIMIT 1;

sql_exec_info.sql: SELECT T1.surname FROM drivers AS T1 INNER JOIN qualifying AS T2 ON T1.driverId = T2.driverId WHERE T2.raceId = 19 AND T2.q2 = (SELECT MIN(q2) FROM qualifying WHERE raceId = 19 AND q2 IS NOT NULL)

selected_schemas.chain_of_thought_reasoning: To calculate the percentage, I need to: 1) Filter races where Hamilton participated since 2010, 2) Count races where Hamilton did *not* come in 1st, 3) Count all races Hamilton participated in since 2010, and 4) Divide the results. The driver's surname and race year are needed for filtering and counting races. The result's position is needed to determine whether Hamilton was in first place or not. The raceId is needed for counting races and joining tables. The driverRef is needed for joining to get the driver's surname.

The question asks to calculate the percentage of races since 2010 where Hamilton was not in the 1st position, out of all races Hamilton participated in since 2010. 

1. I need to identify races Hamilton participated in. This requires joining `drivers` with `results` and `races`.
2. I need to filter for races after the year 2010. This information is in the `races` table.
3. I need to check Hamilton's surname. This is in the `drivers` table.
4. I need to determine Hamilton's finishing position in each race. This is in the `results` table.
5. I need to count the total number of races Hamilton participated in since 2010.
6. I need to count the number of races Hamilton did *not* finish in 1st position since 2010.
7. Finally, I need to divide the count from step 6 by the count from step 5 to get the percentage. The hint mentions `raceId` for counting, `surname` for filtering by driver, `year` for filtering by date, and `position` for determining the race outcome. The `circuitId` is mentioned in the question but is not directly needed for the calculation based on the hint, as the hint focuses on `raceId`, `year`, and `position`.

sql_exec_info.sql:
SELECT
  CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN T2.position > 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / COUNT(T3.raceId)
FROM drivers AS T1
INNER JOIN results AS T2
  ON T1.driverId = T2.driverId
INNER JOIN races AS T3
  ON T2.raceId = T3.raceId
WHERE
  T1.surname = 'Hamilton' AND T3.year >= 2010;

sql_exec_info.sql:
WITH TargetRace AS (
  SELECT raceId
  FROM races
  WHERE name = 'Australian Grand Prix' AND year = 2008
),
ChampionTime AS (
  SELECT
    CAST(SUBSTR(T1.time, 1, INSTR(T1.time, ':') - 1) AS REAL) * 3600 +
    CAST(SUBSTR(T1.time, INSTR(T1.time, ':') + 1, INSTR(SUBSTR(T1.time, INSTR(T1.time, ':') + 1), ':') - 1) AS REAL) * 60 +
    CAST(SUBSTR(T1.time, INSTR(T1.time, ':', INSTR(T1.time, ':') + 1) + 1) AS REAL) AS champion_seconds
  FROM results AS T1
  INNER JOIN TargetRace AS TR ON T1.raceId = TR.raceId
  WHERE T1.time NOT LIKE '+%'
  ORDER BY champion_seconds ASC
  LIMIT 1
),
MaxIncrementalTime AS (
  SELECT
    MAX(CAST(SUBSTR(T1.time, 2) AS REAL)) AS max_incremental_seconds
  FROM results AS T1
  INNER JOIN TargetRace AS TR ON T1.raceId = TR.raceId
  WHERE T1.time LIKE '+%'
)
SELECT
  (M.max_incremental_seconds * 100.0) / (C.champion_seconds + M.max_incremental_seconds)
FROM ChampionTime AS C, MaxIncrementalTime AS M;

sql_exec_info.sql:
SELECT T1.driverId
        FROM results AS T1
        INNER JOIN races AS T2
          ON T1.raceId = T2.raceId
        WHERE T2.name = 'Canadian Grand Prix' AND T1.statusId = 3
        GROUP BY T1.driverId
        ORDER BY COUNT(T1.resultId) DESC
        LIMIT 1

FROM results AS T1
WHERE T1.statusId = 3 AND T1.raceId = (
    SELECT T1_sub.raceId
    FROM results AS T1_sub
    INNER JOIN races AS T2_sub
      ON T1_sub.raceId = T2_sub.raceId
    WHERE T2_sub.name LIKE '%Canadian Grand Prix%' AND T1_sub.statusId = 3
    GROUP BY T1_sub.raceId
    ORDER BY COUNT(T1_sub.raceId) DESC
    LIMIT 1
);

selected_schemas.chain_of_thought_reasoning: To answer the question, I need to count the number of matches per league and then find the league with the maximum match count. The league name is needed for the output. The league ID is needed to group the matches by league. The Match table is needed to count the matches.

The question asks for the name of the league with the highest number of matches and the count of those matches. To achieve this, I need to: 1. Count the number of matches for each league. The `Match` table contains records of individual matches and has a `league_id` column that links to the `League` table. 2. Identify the league with the maximum count of matches. 3. Retrieve the name of that league from the `League` table. Therefore, I need `league_id` from the `Match` table to group and count matches per league, and `name` from the `League` table to get the league's name. The `id` column in the `League` table is necessary to join with the `Match` table.

sql_exec_info.sql: SELECT T1.name, COUNT(T2.id) FROM League AS T1 INNER JOIN Match AS T2 ON T1.id = T2.league_id GROUP BY T1.name ORDER BY COUNT(T2.id) DESC LIMIT 1

Count the number of matches for each league. The `Match` table contains records of individual matches and has a `league_id` column that links to the `League` table. 2. Identify the league with the maximum count of matches. 3. Retrieve the name of that league from the `League` table. Therefore, I need `league_id` from the `Match` table to group and count matches per league, and `name` from the `League` table to get the league's name. The `id` column in the `League` table is necessary to join with the `Match` table.

sql_exec_info.sql: SELECT T1.name, COUNT(T2.league_id) FROM League AS T1 INNER JOIN Match AS T2 ON T1.id = T2.league_id GROUP BY T1.name ORDER BY COUNT(T2.league_id) DESC LIMIT 1

The question asks for the `team_fifa_api_id` of teams that have a `buildUpPlaySpeed` between 51 and 59. The `Team_Attributes` table contains both `team_fifa_api_id` and `buildUpPlaySpeed`. Therefore, I need to select these two columns from the `Team_Attributes` table and filter based on the `buildUpPlaySpeed` column.

sql_exec_info.sql: SELECT team_fifa_api_id FROM Team_Attributes WHERE buildUpPlaySpeed BETWEEN 51 AND 59

sql_exec_info.sql:
SELECT DISTINCT
  T1.team_long_name
FROM Team AS T1
INNER JOIN Team_Attributes AS T2
  ON T1.team_api_id = T2.team_api_id
WHERE
  STRFTIME('%Y', T2.date) = '2012' AND T2.buildUpPlayPassing > (
    SELECT
      AVG(buildUpPlayPassing)
    FROM Team_Attributes
    WHERE
      STRFTIME('%Y', date) = '2012' AND buildUpPlayPassing IS NOT NULL
  );

FROM Team AS T1
INNER JOIN Team_Attributes AS T2
  ON T1.team_api_id = T2.team_api_id
WHERE
  STRFTIME('%Y', T2.date) = '2012' AND T2.buildUpPlayPassing IS NOT NULL AND T2.buildUpPlayPassing > (
    SELECT
      AVG(T3.buildUpPlayPassing)
    FROM Team_Attributes AS T3
    WHERE
      STRFTIME('%Y', T3.date) = '2012' AND T3.buildUpPlayPassing IS NOT NULL
  );

The team_long_name column is needed to retrieve the team's name. The buildUpPlayPassing and team_fifa_api_id columns are needed to calculate and filter for above-average build-up play passing. The Team_Attributes table provides the buildUpPlayPassing information and the team_fifa_api_id to join with the Team table to get the team's long name. The Team table is required to get the team_long_name.

sql_exec_info.sql:
SELECT DISTINCT T1.team_long_name
FROM Team AS T1
INNER JOIN Team_Attributes AS T2
  ON T1.team_api_id = T2.team_api_id
WHERE
  STRFTIME('%Y', T2.date) = '2012' AND T2.buildUpPlayPassing > (
    SELECT AVG(buildUpPlayPassing)
    FROM Team_Attributes
    WHERE
      STRFTIME('%Y', date) = '2012' AND buildUpPlayPassing IS NOT NULL
  );

This requires retrieving the `team_long_name` from the `Team` table. To filter by build-up play passing and the year 2012, I need to access `buildUpPlayPassing` and potentially a date column (though the hint specifies `strftime('%Y', date) = '2012'`, implying a date is available, but not explicitly shown in the schema for `Team_Attributes` or `Match`. Assuming the year information is implicitly linked to `Team_Attributes` or can be derived from `Match` dates if joined). The hint specifies `buildUpPlayPassing` and the year 2012. The `Team_Attributes` table contains `buildUpPlayPassing`. The `Match` table has a `date` column which can be used to filter by year. The `Team` table is needed for `team_long_name`. Therefore, I need `Team.team_long_name`, `Team_Attributes.buildUpPlayPassing`, and potentially a date column from `Match` to filter by year.

sql_exec_info.sql:
SELECT T1.team_long_name
        FROM Team AS T1
        INNER JOIN Team_Attributes AS T2
          ON T1.team_api_id = T2.team_api_id
        WHERE T1.team_api_id IN (
            SELECT home_team_api_id FROM Match WHERE STRFTIME('%Y', date) = '2012'
            UNION
            SELECT away_team_api_id FROM Match WHERE STRFTIME('%Y', date) = '2012'
        )
        AND T2.buildUpPlayPassing > (
            SELECT AVG(T3.buildUpPlayPassing)
            FROM Team_Attributes AS T3
            WHERE T3.team_api_id IN (
                SELECT home_team_api_id FROM Match WHERE STRFTIME('%Y', date) = '2012'
                UNION
                SELECT away_team_api_id FROM Match WHERE STRFTIME('%Y', date) = '2012'
            ) AND T3.buildUpPlayPassing IS NOT NULL
        );

To filter by build-up play passing and the year 2012, I need to access `buildUpPlayPassing` and potentially a date column (though the hint specifies `strftime('%Y', date) = '2012'`, implying a date is available, but not explicitly shown in the schema for `Team_Attributes` or `Match`. Assuming the year information is implicitly linked to `Team_Attributes` or can be derived from `Match` dates if joined). The hint specifies `buildUpPlayPassing` and the year 2012. The `Team_Attributes` table contains `buildUpPlayPassing`. The `Match` table has a `date` column which can be used to filter by year. The `Team` table is needed for `team_long_name`. Therefore, I need `Team.team_long_name`, `Team_Attributes.buildUpPlayPassing`, and potentially a date column from `Match` to filter by year.

sql_exec_info.sql:
SELECT DISTINCT
  T1.team_long_name
FROM Team AS T1
INNER JOIN Team_Attributes AS T2
  ON T1.team_api_id = T2.team_api_id
WHERE
  STRFTIME('%Y', T2.date) = '2012' AND T2.buildUpPlayPassing > (
    SELECT
      AVG(buildUpPlayPassing)
    FROM Team_Attributes
    WHERE
      STRFTIME('%Y', date) = '2012' AND buildUpPlayPassing IS NOT NULL
  );

selected_schemas.chain_of_thought_reasoning: To answer this question, I need to: 1) Filter players by height > 180, 2) Calculate the average heading accuracy for each player, 3) Sort the players by average heading accuracy in descending order, and 4) Limit the results to the top 10 players. The player_name is required for the output. The height is required for filtering. The heading_accuracy and player_fifa_api_id are needed to calculate the average heading accuracy. The player_fifa_api_id is required to group the results for calculating the average.

The question asks for the top 10 players' names whose heights are above 180, ordered by their average heading accuracy. This requires filtering players by height, calculating the average heading accuracy for each player, and then ordering them. The 'Player' table contains player names and their heights. The 'Player_Attributes' table contains heading accuracy and a player identifier to link with the 'Player' table. Therefore, 'player_name' and 'height' from the 'Player' table, and 'heading_accuracy' and 'player_fifa_api_id' (to join with Player and aggregate) from 'Player_Attributes' are needed.

sql_exec_info.sql: SELECT T1.player_name FROM Player AS T1 INNER JOIN Player_Attributes AS T2 ON T1.player_api_id = T2.player_api_id WHERE T1.height > 180 GROUP BY T1.player_name ORDER BY AVG(T2.heading_accuracy) DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 10

schema_representation.execution_plan: Execution plan: To answer this question, I need to: 1) Filter players by height > 180, 2) Calculate the average heading accuracy for each player, 3) Sort the players by average heading accuracy in descending order, and 4) Limit the results to the top 10 players. The player_name is required for the output. The height is required for filtering. The heading_accuracy and player_fifa_api_id are needed to calculate the average heading accuracy. The player_fifa_api_id is required to group the results for calculating the average.

sql_exec_info.sql:
SELECT T1.player_name
FROM Player AS T1
INNER JOIN Player_Attributes AS T2
  ON T1.player_fifa_api_id = T2.player_fifa_api_id
WHERE
  T1.height > 180
GROUP BY
  T1.player_name
ORDER BY
  AVG(T2.heading_accuracy) DESC
LIMIT 10;

selected_schemas.chain_of_thought_reasoning: To answer this question, I need to: 1) Find the country Germany, 2) Find the leagues associated with the country Germany. The Country table is needed to filter for Germany. The League table is needed to retrieve league names. The Match table and associated foreign keys are not needed to answer the question because we are not looking for anything about a match.

The question asks to list leagues from Germany. The hint specifies that 'Germany' refers to `Country.name`. The `Match` table has a `country_id` and `league_id` which link to the `Country` and `League` tables respectively. To find leagues from Germany, I need to join `League` with `Country` on their respective IDs and then filter by `Country.name` being 'Germany'. The `League.name` column is what the question asks to list.

sql_exec_info.sql: SELECT T1.name FROM League AS T1 INNER JOIN Country AS T2 ON T1.country_id = T2.id WHERE T2.name = 'Germany'

selected_schemas.chain_of_thought_reasoning: The question requires filtering players based on their height and volley score. The question asks to count players based on two criteria: height and volley score. The `Player` table contains the `height` column, and the `Player_Attributes` table contains the `volleys` column. Therefore, I need to join these two tables on a common player identifier. The `player_api_id` is the foreign key linking `Player_Attributes` to `Player`. I will filter players with `height` greater than 180 and `volleys` greater than 70, and then count the resulting players.

sql_exec_info.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT T1.player_api_id) FROM Player AS T1 INNER JOIN Player_Attributes AS T2 ON T1.player_api_id = T2.player_api_id WHERE T1.height > 180 AND T2.volleys > 70

The hint specifies that 'Ajax's' refers to `team_long_name = 'Ajax'`, 'chance creation passing score' refers to `MAX(chanceCreationPassing)`, and 'classified as' refers to `chanceCreationPassingClass`. Therefore, I need to join the `Team` table (to filter by `team_long_name`) with the `Team_Attributes` table (to get `chanceCreationPassing` and `chanceCreationPassingClass`). schema_representation.execution_plan: Execution plan: The question asks to identify players who 'tend to be attacking when their mates were doing attack moves'. The hint clarifies that 'tend to be attacking when their mates were doing attack moves' translates to `attacking_work_rate = 'high'`. Therefore, I need to find players whose `attacking_work_rate` is 'high'. The player's name is requested in the output. The `Player` table contains `player_name` and `player_api_id`. The `Player_Attributes` table contains `attacking_work_rate` and `player_api_id` (which links to the `Player` table). So, I need to join `Player` and `Player_Attributes` on `player_api_id` and filter `Player_Attributes` by `attacking_work_rate = 'high'`, then select the `player_name` from the `Player` table.

sql_exec_info.sql: SELECT DISTINCT T1.player_name FROM Player AS T1 INNER JOIN Player_Attributes AS T2 ON T1.player_api_id = T2.player_api_id WHERE T2.attacking_work_rate = 'high'

selected_schemas.chain_of_thought_reasoning: To answer this question, I need to: 1) Filter patients born in 1937, 2) Find their total cholesterol, and 3) Filter for total cholesterol values beyond the normal range (>= 250). The Birthday column is needed to filter for the birth year. The T-CHO column is needed to check for the cholesterol level. The ID column is needed to join the tables.

The question asks to list patients born in 1937 who have total cholesterol beyond the normal range. To achieve this, I need to: 1. Filter patients by their birth year to select those born in 1937. The 'Birthday' column in the 'Patient' table is required for this. 2. Identify patients whose 'T-CHO' (total cholesterol) is greater than or equal to '250'. This information is in the 'Laboratory' table. 3. Join the 'Patient' and 'Laboratory' tables on the 'ID' column to link patient birth dates with their laboratory results. 4. Select the patient IDs that satisfy both conditions. Therefore, 'Patient.ID', 'Patient.Birthday', 'Laboratory.ID', and 'Laboratory.T-CHO' are the necessary columns.

sql_exec_info.sql: SELECT DISTINCT T1.ID FROM Patient AS T1 INNER JOIN Laboratory AS T2 ON T1.ID = T2.ID WHERE STRFTIME('%Y', T1.Birthday) = '1937' AND T2."T-CHO" >= 250

The question asks for the highest total bilirubin level and the details of the patient(s) who recorded that level. To find the highest total bilirubin, I need to look at the 'T-BIL' column in the 'Laboratory' table and use the MAX aggregate function. To list the patient details (ID, sex, and birthday), I need to join the 'Laboratory' table with the 'Patient' table using the 'ID' column. The question asks for the name and location of events that underspend their budget. To determine if an event underspends its budget, I need to check the 'remaining' amount in the 'budget' table. If 'remaining' is greater than 0, it means the budget is underspent. The 'event_name' and 'location' are attributes of the 'event' table. To link budget information to events, I need to join the 'budget' table with the 'event' table using the 'link_to_event' column in the 'budget' table and the 'event_id' (implicitly represented by the FK relationship) in the 'event' table. Therefore, I need 'event_name' and 'location' from the 'event' table, and 'remaining' and 'link_to_event' from the 'budget' table. The hint confirms that 'remaining > 0' indicates underspending and 'event_name' is the name of the event.

selected_schemas.chain_of_thought_reasoning: To answer this question, I need to: 1) Calculate the average parking cost, 2) Identify events with parking costs less than the calculated average, and 3) List the names of those events. The 'event' table contains the event names. The 'budget' table contains the budgeted cost and the link to the event. The 'expense' table provides the actual cost. The 'category' in the 'budget' table is needed to filter for parking costs. The link between 'expense' and 'budget' is necessary to link expense cost to the budget category.

The question asks to list event names with less than the average parking cost. The hint specifies that 'name of events' refers to 'event_name' and 'less than average parking cost' refers to 'cost < DIVIDE(SUM(cost), COUNT(event_id)) where category = 'Parking''. This implies we need to: 1. Identify events with a 'Parking' category from the 'budget' table. 2. Calculate the average cost for these parking expenses. 3. Join the 'budget' table with the 'event' table to get the event names. 4. Filter for events where the parking cost is less than the calculated average. Therefore, we need 'event_name' from the 'event' table, and 'link_to_event', 'category', and 'spent' from the 'budget' table to link events to their parking costs and calculate the average. The hint mentions 'event_id' for the average calculation, but the 'budget' table uses 'link_to_event' which is a foreign key to 'event_id'. Thus, 'link_to_event' in 'budget' and 'event_id' in 'event' are implicitly needed for the join. However, since the question focuses on the 'name of events' and the hint directly links 'event_id' to the cost calculation, and 'budget' table has 'link_to_event' that links to 'event_id', we need to select 'event_name' from 'event' and 'link_to_event', 'category', and 'spent' from 'budget'. The hint also implies that the 'budget_id' is implicitly used in the expense table to link to budget, but the question is about cost and event names, not individual expenses. Therefore, the essential columns are `event_name` from `event` and `link_to_event`, `category`, and `spent` from `budget`.

sql_exec_info.sql: SELECT DISTINCT T1.event_name FROM event AS T1 INNER JOIN budget AS T2 ON T1.event_id = T2.link_to_event WHERE T2.category = 'Parking' AND T2.spent < (SELECT AVG(spent) FROM budget WHERE category = 'Parking')

schema_representation.execution_plan: Execution plan: To answer this question, I need to: 1) Calculate the average parking cost, 2) Identify events with parking costs less than the calculated average, and 3) List the names of those events. The 'event' table contains the event names. The 'budget' table contains the budgeted cost and the link to the event. The 'expense' table provides the actual cost. The 'category' in the 'budget' table is needed to filter for parking costs. The link between 'expense' and 'budget' is necessary to link expense cost to the budget category.

sql_exec_info.sql:
SELECT
  T1.event_name
FROM event AS T1
JOIN budget AS T2
  ON T1.event_id = T2.link_to_event
JOIN expense AS T3
  ON T2.budget_id = T3.link_to_budget
WHERE
  T2.category = 'Parking'
GROUP BY
  T1.event_name
HAVING
  SUM(T3.cost) < (
    SELECT
      AVG(T4.cost)
    FROM expense AS T4
    JOIN budget AS T5
      ON T4.link_to_budget = T5.budget_id
    WHERE
      T5.category = 'Parking'
  );

The question asks for the 'full name' and the 'college' of club members who have the 'position' of 'Secretary'. The 'full name' can be obtained from the 'first_name' column in the 'member' table. The 'position' is also in the 'member' table and will be used for filtering. The 'college' is in the 'major' table, and since the 'member' table has a foreign key 'link_to_major' that references 'major.major_id', we need to join these two tables. The 'member_id' is the primary key for the 'member' table and is used as the foreign key in the 'major' table (implicitly, as 'link_to_major' references 'major_id', though 'major_id' is not explicitly defined in the schema, it's implied by the foreign key constraint). The 'major_name' and 'department' columns in the 'major' table are not directly needed for the output or filtering. The 'college' column in the 'major' table is needed for the output. Therefore, I need 'first_name' and 'position' from the 'member' table, and 'college' from the 'major' table. I also need the foreign key 'link_to_major' from the 'member' table to join with the 'major' table.

sql_exec_info.sql: SELECT T1.first_name, T1.last_name, T2.college FROM member AS T1 INNER JOIN major AS T2 ON T1.link_to_major = T2.major_id WHERE T1.position = 'Secretary'
